problem:
Calculate the product ${I}_{3}B$ given that ${I}_{3}$ is the $3\times 3$ identity matrix and
$B=[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 & 3 \\ 2 & 0 & -6 \\ -5 & 7 & 1\end{aligned}].$

|  |  | {{field-1}} | {{field-2}} | {{field-3}} |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${I}_{3}\cdot B=\,\,$ |  | {{field-4}} | {{field-5}} | {{field-6}} |  |
|  |  | {{field-7}} | {{field-8}} | {{field-9}} |  |
worked_solution:
Any matrix, when multiplied by an identity matrix, remains unchanged (assuming that the multiplication is well defined).

The matrix $B$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix and ${I}_{3}$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix too. 

Therefore, the multiplication is well defined and 

$$
{I}_{3}\cdot B=B=[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 & 3 \\ 2 & 0 & -6 \\ -5 & 7 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$
